blocks.text: A year after revealing a Miss Piggy movie in the works, Jennifer Lawrence has shared an update on the Muppet solo outing.

The Oscar-winning actress, who is developing the project with fellow producer Emma Stone and screenwriter Cole Escola , teased the status of the script in response to a fan question on Watch What Happens Live .
“I don’t know! I always get in trouble for saying stuff,” said Lawrence, before reluctantly sharing: “Um, we have a first draft!”

blocks.text: Last November, Lawrence first announced on Las Culturistas that she and 2x Oscar winner Stone were developing the movie with Tony-winning Oh, Mary! sensation Escola penning the script, marking the character’s first solo outing since Jim Henson debuted her on The Muppet Show in 1976.
When asked if the trio would appear in the film, Lawrence said, “I think so, we have to.”

Shortly after, Lawrence recounted how they decided to give the “feminist icon” her own movie . “So, during lockdown, one of my good friends who is not in the industry—it was also kind of around cancel culture. It was like both things were kind of happening at once. We were all locked up in our rooms, naughty people were being locked up in prison,” she recalled.

links.text: give the “feminist icon” her own movie

blocks.text: Lawrence explained, “Miss Piggy is a feminist icon, and she said it would be so funny if Miss Piggy got canceled. Now, that is not the plot, necessarily, but it got the wheels turning.”

Noting “there hasn’t actually been” a solo project about Miss Piggy, Lawrence added, “So, I started kind of producing it. But Emma Stone is the Muppet-head. Also, Emma Stone is a shark … I’m, just like, the ideas guy. So, I went to her to be like, ‘What do we do?’ So, now Cole is writing it, and they’re perfect.”

Starting as a chorus pig on The Muppet Show in the mid-1970s, Miss Piggy gradually became a bigger part of the series, before becoming an icon in the late ’70s and early ’80s. Despite Kermit being the star, she’s long hogged the spotlight from her froggy beau.
